result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 5 pass / 0 fail across 3 files.

`POST /login` is now throttled to 5 submissions per client per minute. The new `app/Http/Middleware/ThrottleLogin.ts` wraps the framework's `createRateLimitMiddleware` with a dedicated in-memory `MemoryRateLimitStore`, a 5-per-60s budget, and `trustProxy: false`, so the client identity is the connection's own address via `server.requestIP()` and forwarded-for style headers are ignored; when no address is available the limiter falls back to a single shared per-route bucket, so unidentifiable clients are counted together rather than let through. It exposes an injectable `now` clock purely so tests can step past the window. `routes/web.ts` registers it as the named `throttle.login` alias next to the existing `auth`/`guest` aliases (named, so `guren audit` can still see the chain), and `routes/auth.ts` moves `POST /login` out of the guest group into its own registration with `.middleware('throttle.login', 'guest')` — the throttle therefore runs ahead of the guest guard, so a client over its limit gets 429 regardless of what its session says, including a submission with the correct password. Every submission counts, successes included, and the count is never reset on success; the 6th and later requests in a window get HTTP 429 plus a `Retry-After` header in seconds, and the client is allowed through again once the window rolls over. `GET /login`, registration, and every other route are untouched. `tests/LoginThrottle.test.ts` covers the 429 + `Retry-After` on the sixth attempt through the real app, that a throttled client can still load `/login` and `/health` and reach `POST /register`, and — on an isolated app with a fake clock — that submissions are allowed again after the window passes.
